a suit being Title Suit no. 45 of 2000, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kotalipara praying inter alia, decree for permanent injunction against the defendant-opposite party nos. 1 to 6 and also filed an application under Order XXXIX rules l and 2 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for an order of temporary injunction till disposed of the suit with a further prayer for ad-interim injunction whereupon a notice to show cause was issued upon the defendants. The defendants on appearing in the suit filed a written objection to the prayer for temporary injunction. On hearing the parties, the learned Assistant Judge by his order dated 03.02.2002, rejected the said application for temporary injunction, as such, an appeal being 

 "115. Revision.-(1) The High Court Division may, on the application of any party aggrieved, call for the record of any suit or proceeding , in which a decree or an order has been passed by a Court of District Judge or Additional District Judge, or a decree has been passed by a Court of Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge, from which no appeal lies; and if such Court appears to have committed any error of law resulting in an error in such decree or order occasioning failure of justice, the High Court Division may, revise such decree or order and, make such order in the suit or proceeding, as it thinks fit. (2) The Court of District Judge may, on the application of any party aggrieved, call for the record of any suit or proceeding, in which an order has been passed by a court of Joint District Judge. Senior Assistant Judge or 

 District Judge or an Additional District Judge, appears to have committed any error of law resulting in an error in such decree or order, occasioning a failure of justice, the High Court Division, on the application of any aggrieved party, may call for the record of any such suit of proceeding in which a decree or an order passed by those Courts, may revise such decree or order and make such order in the suit or proceeding as it thinks fit. The High Court Division may also exercise such powers of revision in respect of the decree passed by the Court of Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge, from which no appeal lies, but in this later category the word 'order' is omitted. Obviously, the orders passed by the Court of Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge and the Assistant Judge, are kept outside the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division. 

 the said order in appeal, in affirming, the order of the original court, It is also not denied that the said order is not a decree as mentioned in the second part of sub-section I of Section 115 of the Code but is an order although passed in appeal. This order is sought to be challenged under section 115(1) of the Code. 

 8. Mr. Gobinda Chandra Tagore, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that in this case a petition has been filed under Order XXX IX rules I and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge and on appeal, the order rejecting prayer for temporary injunction was affirmed and since this order was passed in appeal by the Joint District Judge, though not a decree in a proper sense but it is very much similar to that of a decree. Since this order was passed by the Court in its appellate capacity, this order which could have been passed by the Di5trict Judge or an Additional District Judge, although not a decree but should be treated at par a decree. 

 10. Sub-Section I of Section 115 of the Code, as amended, confers the revisional power 'upon the High Court Division in respect of the decree and order both, if passed by the District Judge and the Additional District Judge, and also in respect of the decree (not order) if passed by the Joint District Judge, the Senior Assistant Judge or the Assistant Judge, where there is no appeal.
